help.title: How Weight Learning Works
help.step1_desc: Each time you pick a winner, the system learns your preferences using the Bradley-Terry model, which calculates a "true quality score" for each photo based on win/loss patterns.
help.step2_title: 2. Suggest Weights optimizes the weight combination
help.step2_desc: The algorithm finds the best ratio of weights that makes the combined score match your preferences. It uses mathematical optimization (SLSQP) to maximize how well the weighted sum predicts your choices.
help.step3_positive: Positive correlation (+0.5 to +1.0) = weights rank photos similar to your preferences
help.step3_zero: Near zero (-0.2 to +0.2) = not enough data or mixed signals
help.step3_negative: Negative correlation = weights rank opposite to your preferences
help.step4_title: 4. Apply to save, Recalculate to update
help.step4_desc: Click "Apply to Config" to save weights, then "Recalculate Scores" to update all photo scores in the database.

weights.title: Category Weights
weights.radar_help: Each axis represents one of the 12 scoring dimensions. The polygon's shape shows how much each dimension contributes to the aggregate score for that category. A wider polygon means more dimensions are weighted heavily. Comparing polygons reveals which categories emphasize similar dimensions (overlapping shapes) or have very different scoring strategies (different shapes). Select up to 5 categories to compare.
weights.heatmap_help: A matrix of all categories (rows) and scoring dimensions (columns). Cell brightness indicates the weight percentage — brighter green means a higher contribution to the aggregate. This gives a bird's-eye view to spot patterns: which dimensions are universally important, which are category-specific, and where weights might need rebalancing.
weights.editor_intro: Edit how the aggregate score is computed for a category. Each dimension's score (0-10) is multiplied by its weight percentage, then summed to produce the final aggregate. Modifiers apply additional bonuses or penalty adjustments.
weights.weights_hint: How much each dimension contributes to the aggregate score. Should total 100% for a balanced weighted average.
weights.save_note: Updates config file. Recompute to apply to all photos in this category.
weights.corr_hint: Compares your slider weights (blue) against actual Pearson correlation with aggregate score (green/red). Mismatches reveal dimensions with high weight but low real impact, or vice versa.
weights.preview_hint: Estimated aggregate score distribution with the current slider values compared to actual scores.
weights.modifiers_hint: Fine-tune scoring behavior beyond the weighted average. Multipliers scale penalties (0.5 = half penalty, 2 = double). Bonuses are added to the final score.

correlations.title: Score-Weight Correlations
correlations.heatmap_help: Pearson r measures how much a dimension's raw score actually moves in sync with the aggregate score (-1 to +1). Green = positive correlation (higher dimension score leads to higher aggregate), red = negative. A bright cell means strong influence. Compare this to your configured weights: if a dimension has high weight but low correlation, it may not be differentiating photos effectively in that category.
correlations.detail_help: Side-by-side comparison for one category. The green bars show the weight you configured (as %), the blue bars show the actual Pearson correlation. Look for mismatches: a tall green bar with a short blue bar means you're weighting a dimension heavily but it has little real impact on score variation. A tall blue bar with a short green bar means an influential dimension is under-weighted.

help.breakdown: Shows how your photos are distributed across categories. The bar chart displays photo counts per category sorted by volume. Select a category from the dropdown to see its average scores across dimensions and the aggregate score distribution histogram.
help.weights: Each category has 12 weight dimensions that control how the aggregate score is calculated. The radar chart lets you visually compare weight profiles across up to 5 categories. The heatmap gives a full overview of all categories at a glance. In edition mode, you can adjust weights with sliders (should sum to 100%) and modify scoring modifiers like bonus points or penalty toggles.
help.correlations: Shows how strongly each weight dimension actually correlates with the aggregate score using Pearson r (-1 to +1). Green cells indicate positive correlation, red cells negative. Click a category row to see a side-by-side comparison of configured weight % versus actual correlation - this highlights misalignments where a high weight has low impact or vice versa.
help.overlap: Categories are evaluated in priority order - a photo is assigned to the first matching category. This tab shows which category filters overlap: the top table lists pairs of categories whose filters both match the same photos. The summary table shows how many photos match each filter versus how many are actually assigned (the difference being captured by higher-priority categories).

metric_help.score_range: Overall score: the weighted aggregate of all metrics for the photo's category (0–10).
metric_help.aesthetic_range: How pleasing the photo looks overall, scored by TOPIQ (CLIP+MLP on the legacy and 8gb profiles), 0–10.
metric_help.quality_score_range: Technical image quality, scored by TOPIQ NR on the 16gb and 24gb profiles (0–10).
metric_help.aesthetic_iaa_range: Artistic merit, scored by TOPIQ IAA trained on AVA (0–10); separate from technical quality. Best for art and creative shots.
metric_help.face_quality_iqa_range: Quality of the face region, scored by TOPIQ NR-Face (0–10). A photo with no face has no value.
metric_help.liqe_range: Overall image quality, scored by LIQE (0–10), which also diagnoses distortions such as motion blur, overexposure and noise.
metric_help.qrealign_range: Aesthetic score from Q-ReAlign (0–10). On by default on the 8gb, 16gb and 24gb profiles.
metric_help.aesthetic_v25_range: Aesthetic appeal, scored by Aesthetic Predictor v2.5 (0–10). Off by default and deprecated in favour of Q-ReAlign.
metric_help.deqa_range: Image quality, scored by DeQA-Score (0–10). Off by default.
metric_help.face_count_range: Number of faces InsightFace detected in the photo.
metric_help.face_quality_range: Clarity of the faces (detail and expression), from InsightFace face analysis (0–10).
metric_help.eye_sharpness_range: How sharp the eye regions are, measured around InsightFace landmarks (0–10).
metric_help.face_sharpness_range: How sharp the face region is (0–10).
metric_help.face_ratio_range: Share of the frame covered by the largest face (0–1); 0.05 means 5%.
metric_help.face_confidence_range: How confident InsightFace is that the detection is a face (0–1).
metric_help.composition_range: Framing and visual balance, scored by SAMP-Net (rule-based on the CPU profile), 0–10.
metric_help.power_point_range: How well the subject sits on the rule-of-thirds power points (0–10).
metric_help.leading_lines_range: Strength of the lines that lead the eye through the frame, found by edge detection (0–10).
metric_help.isolation_range: How well the subject stands apart from its background (0–10).
metric_help.subject_sharpness_range: Focus quality of the subject compared with the background, from BiRefNet saliency (0–10). A photo with no subject has no value.
metric_help.subject_prominence_range: Share of the frame the subject fills, from BiRefNet (0–10). High for macro and tight framing.
metric_help.subject_placement_range: Rule-of-thirds score for the subject's centre of mass, from BiRefNet (0–10).
metric_help.bg_separation_range: Edge-gradient difference at the subject boundary, a proxy for bokeh quality, from BiRefNet (0–10).
metric_help.moment_confidence_range: How confident the photo's narrative-moment label is (0–1).
metric_help.sharpness_range: Overall technical sharpness, from Laplacian variance (0–10).
metric_help.exposure_range: Exposure balance from the histogram, with a penalty for clipping (0–10).
metric_help.noise_range: Estimated sensor noise (sigma, 0–20); lower is cleaner.
metric_help.dynamic_range: Tonal range from shadows to highlights, from the histogram.
metric_help.histogram_range: How widely the tones spread across the histogram; a narrow spread means a flat, low-contrast image.
metric_help.channel_clip_highlight_range: Percentage of pixels clipped to white in their worst RGB channel. Unknown until clipping has been backfilled or the photo rescanned.
metric_help.channel_clip_shadow_range: Percentage of pixels clipped to black in their worst RGB channel. Unknown until clipping has been backfilled or the photo rescanned.
metric_help.aperture_range: Aperture f-number, from EXIF; lower means a wider aperture.
metric_help.focal_range: Lens focal length in millimetres, from EXIF.
metric_help.quality_tier: Quality grade derived from the aggregate score: excellent, good, fair or poor.
metric_help.color_temp: Overall colour cast of the photo: warm, cool or neutral.
metric_help.hue_bucket: Dominant hue of the photo, grouped into eight colour families.

culling.help_text: Cull near-duplicate shots fast. Pick a granularity — Bursts, Similar, Scenes, or All merged — and a sort order; Strictness sets how aggressively the auto-selection keeps only the best frame, and in Similar mode the Similarity slider tunes how alike photos must be to group. Click a photo to keep or unkeep it, double-click to keep only that one, or turn on the Loupe (Z) to pixel-peep. Open the Darkroom (Enter) for full-screen review with 2-up/4-up Compare. Use Up/Down to pick a group and Space to confirm it and move on; Skip and Confirm start a 7-second cooldown you can Cancel before the group closes, and confirming hides the rejected photos from the gallery. Scope the feed to an album or scene, toggle Exclude rejected, and note that every cull decision trains your personal "My Taste" ranking. See the shortcuts below for all keys.

Arrow keys browse photos; use the zoom button, scroll or double-click the preview to zoom. R rejects the focused photo immediately and excludes it from the draft. Undo restores its review and draft membership. Grouping waits for Save; leaving without saving does not undo Reject.

related_files.help: Photo display requests this indexed file; the rendition indicator reports what actually decoded. Gallery thumbnails are stored previews. Same-stem RAW/JPEG and XMP names are candidates, not proof of identity. Manual stacks are separate. RAW download follows the existing companion rule; sidecar import and export use their own naming policies. This list is a read-time check, not a file-write preview. Linked targets are not inspected. Only supported lower/upper-case RAW/JPEG extensions and the three shown XMP naming patterns are checked.
